description:
We are happy to announce that our 2021 Summer Reading Program has started here at the Mokena Library! We have programs for Children (Ages Infant - 5th Grade), Junior High (Ages 6th - 8th Grade), High School students and Adults. 

The theme for the Children's Summer Reading Program is "Reading Colors Your World!" To celebrate the kick off to Summer Read, and to go along with this year's colorful and fun theme, our Children's Librarian, Ms. Emily, will be reading "The Artist Who Painted a Blue Horse" by Eric Carle. This is cute book featuring lots of different animals and colors. 

To register for our Summer Reading Program, click on the link below using Beanstack. Once registered for this year's Summer Reading Program, you can pick up a registration bag with all of the goodies featured in this video, while supplies last. 
https://mokenalibrary.beanstack.org/reader365

To see all of the fun events and programs we have planned here at the Mokena Library, you can visit our events calendar on our website, or read our Summer Read Newsletter, both linked here.

Some thought this book was psychologically damaging and traumatizing to young children and called for its removal. 

[Video description: Children's Librarian Miss Andrea starts the video with wiggles, doing each action she says. She then reads today's book, which features a child in monster pajamas and actual monsters living on an island. After the book. author: Mem Fox, Kathryn Brown
video_title: Virtual Storytime: 'Tough Boris'
description:
Yo ho, Tough Boris is mean and scary  - and an animal lover! This week's story is "Tough Boris" by Mem Fox and illustrated by Kathryn Brown.

[Video description: Children's Librarian Miss Andrea starts the video with wiggles, doing each action when she says it. She then reads this week's book, holding it up so the viewer can see the pictures. The illustrations feature a pirate with a colorful parrot friend. The pirate also has a violin in many of the drawings, and then it is being slipped out the window by an unseen person. The pirate grabs his sword and tries to find whoever stole his instrument. He finds a boy below decks who stole it! The boy then plays music for all of the pirates. When the parrot dies, the pirate is sad and has a funeral at sea for the bird. After the story, Miss Andrea gets up and acts out the song she sings. She ends the video with the goodbye song.]

[Video description: Children's Librarian Miss Andrea is surrounded by circus items like trapeze swings, unicycles, ladders, and stilts. She reads the book, which features a little elefant and many words that start with thefirst part of "elephant". Each picture has a word, and shows the elephant doing something related to the word. The first word, eleph-ate, shows the baby elephant eating bananas. Next are ele-vated and ele-fate, where the elephant is pulled up into a tree by a net trap. Each word describes what happened to the elephant. After reading the book, Miss Andrea claps the goodbye song.]

author: David LaRochelle, Mike Wohnoutka
video_title: Virtual Storytime: 'Moo!'
description:
Check out this cow-tstanding story from David LaRochelle and Mike Wohnoutka: "Moo!"

[Video description: Children's Librarian Miss Andrea starts the video with wiggles, wiggling each part as she says to wiggle it. She then reads the book, holding it up for the audience to see. The book features a cow, who jumps into the farmer's vehicle after seeing it for sale. The cow rides the car up and down many hills. It looks very happy as it drives. It then sees a warning sign in the road and looks scared. Then it covers its eyes as it hits a huge rock, goes flying, and crashes on top of another vehicle. It's a police vehicle! And the officer is not happy. The cow tries to explain what happened, all in moooooos. The officer points for the cow to leave, still looking angry. The cow walks sadly over all the hills it drove on. The farmer is standing with his arms crossed angrily when the cow gets home. The cow tries to blame a nearby sheep! Once Andrea is done reading, she says animal noises and holds up a paper horse, a paper sheep, a paper dog, a paper cat, a paper chicken, and a paper cow. Then she claps and waves, rhymes, and says goodbye.]

Miss Andrea then sings a song while doing sign language for the lyrics, and then ends the video with clapping and waving goodbye.]
